item.text: The two defects meet in `wordpress.FillWordPress`: it dereferences a pointer to the cache map and reads the global ignore flag. I’ll make cache values nil-safe, pass the per-server WordPress settings through the report integration, and retain the existing `Status`-based inactive filter.

# Checkpoint

Task: resolve WordPress vulnerability cache lookup indirection and inactive package filtering.

Findings:
- "'`wordpress.searchCache` currently takes `*map[string]string`; `FillWordPress` dereferences it at lookup and cache writes.
- `FillWordPress` reads `config.Conf.WpIgnoreInactive` (global) even though the report path already has the per-server `WordPressConf` available.
- Inactive filtering already examines `WpPackage.Status`; `removeInactives` drops `inactive` entries and preserves active entries, while report filtering uses the per-server setting.
- Cache values must allow nil to satisfy the requested nil-entry behavior, so the cache will use `map[string]*string` and lookup will treat absent and nil values as misses.

Planned edits:
- Pass `config.WordPressConf` and a direct `map[string]*string` into WordPress scanning.
- Make cache lookup nil-safe and direct; update cache writes/call sites.
- Extend the existing cache tests for a nil cached pointer and keep Status filtering coverage.
- Run the existing WordPress and report relevant tests.
EOF

Next I’m formatting and running the WordPress, config, and report test packages.

item.text:
Implemented the WordPress cache and filtering changes.

- [wordpress.go](/app/wordpress/wordpress.go) now looks up a direct cache map; missing keys and nil cached pointers return `("", false)`. Scanning uses the supplied per-server `WordPressConf` to filter packages by `Status`.
- [report.go](/app/report/report.go) passes each server’s WordPress configuration into the scan.
- [config.go](/app/config/config.go) now maps `ignoreInactive` from TOML.
- Updated cache tests to cover nil cached values.

`GOPROXY=off go test ./wordpress ./config ./report` passed. The report build emitted a SQLite C compiler warning, but its tests passed.
